title: How Lebanon Became the Middle East’s Battleground
gist: Jackie Northam reviews Kim Ghattas's 'The Best Kind of American', which argues today's Middle East conflicts were set in 1980s Lebanon — notably Israel's 1982 invasion, which birthed Hezbollah — told through the 1984 murder of AUB president Malcolm Kerr; the review links this to the current ninth-month U.S.-Israel war on Iran, in which Israel's renewed Lebanon offensive has killed at least 4,300 and Iran's Strait of Hormuz leverage has caused a global energy crunch while Hezbollah rebuilds.

themes.theme: 1982 invasion as origin of today's conflicts

insights.claim: Kim Ghattas contends that many of the Middle East's current policies and conflicts were established in 1980s Lebanon, particularly through Israel's 1982 invasion, a view the reviewer calls prescient given Israel's push for security and land, Iran's use of Hezbollah, and Lebanon's fragility.
insights.speaker: Jackie Northam
insights.so_what: Historical lens suggests Lebanon cycles of invasion and proxy rebuilding persist, implying chronic regional risk premium.
